title: Getting Over the Abyss
speaker: Mr. Chen
source_note: Adapted from the bridge article concepts: early crossings, bridge parts, construction types, and how shapes carry load.

slides.title: Crossing the Dry Wash
slides.body: A crossing is a promise: weight must find ground again.
slides.mr_chen_line: A crossing is a promise: weight must find ground again.
slides.prompt: Place the bridge deck across the wash.
slides.takeaway: A bridge gives force a path from traveler to ground.

slides.title: Six Ways Across
slides.body: Beam bridges bend. Arches squeeze. Cables pull. Trusses mix forces through triangles.
slides.mr_chen_line: Different bridges solve the same problem with different forces.
slides.prompt: Sort each bridge sketch by its main force behavior.
slides.takeaway: Bridge shape decides where bending, squeezing, and pulling go.

slides.title: Name the Parts
slides.body: The deck or superstructure carries the bike. Abutments and piers carry the deck.
slides.mr_chen_line: A bridge is easier to fix when you can name what carries what.
slides.prompt: Label deck, abutments, and pier on Mr. Chen's clipboard.
slides.takeaway: Deck carries the bike. Abutments and piers carry the deck.

slides.title: The Wobble Problem
slides.body: A rectangle can look strong until the side push arrives.
slides.mr_chen_line: A rectangle can look strong until the side push arrives.
slides.takeaway: Rectangles can fold sideways into a parallelogram.

slides.title: Add the Brace
slides.body: A diagonal brace turns the wobble into triangles.
slides.mr_chen_line: A diagonal brace turns the wobble into triangles.
slides.prompt: Place the diagonal brace, then push again.
slides.takeaway: Triangles lock shape because the sides cannot slide without changing length.

slides.title: Trace the Load
slides.body: Now follow the bike's weight all the way down.
slides.mr_chen_line: Now follow the bike's weight all the way down.
slides.prompt: Tap the load path: deck, braces, supports, ground.
slides.takeaway: Triangles keep a bridge from folding. A good bridge sends the bike's weight from the deck, through braces, into supports, and down to the ground.

takeaway: Strong bridge design is shape plus support: a triangle truss gives the load a path from deck to braces to supports to ground.
